verdict: NOT READY — FR and ID-space integrity are clean and all five rulings are applied structurally, but two pinned acceptance numbers do not survive a count against the Android source, one safety-limits path carries two mutually exclusive requirements, and §7 publishes a disclosure-completeness claim its own rows contradict.
blocking: NFR-30's two pinned accessibility parity counts are grep-token artifacts, not counts of the things they name, and the PRD makes them unreachable acceptance criteria. Counted directly against android-unofficial over app/src/main + wear-device/src/main: `testTag` yields 253 total token occurrences, but only 205 of them are `.testTag(...)` call sites — 28 are `import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag` and 20 are parameter declarations, KDoc comments and named arguments into helper composables. Distinct identifier strings are 188 inline literals plus 9 named-argument strings plus 5 constant references, i.e. roughly 195-200 once the one genuine duplicate (`pairing_fault`, two sites, one string) is split in two as NFR-30 requires. `contentDescription` yields 113 total occurrences, of which 8 are imports and **55 are `contentDescription = null`** — elements deliberately hidden from the accessibility tree; only 50 carry an actual description. NFR-30 (6-nfrs.md:709-720) states '253 accessibility identifiers and 113 combined VoiceOver descriptions ... ported one-for-one from the 253 Compose `testTag` and 113 `contentDescription` call sites', declares them 'the acceptance substrate for every Simulator-runnable gate' and says 'A shortfall against either number is a shortfall in the project's only self-serve verification'; FR-177 (5.9-onboarding-settings.md:662) makes it a completion criterion — 'The registry is complete only when it reaches NFR-30's identifier count'; FR-208 (5.11-engineering-gates.md:201) quotes 253 into the merge-gating registry check. Building to these figures means either a registry that can never close, or ~50 invented identifiers and ~63 invented descriptions — and porting the 55 `= null` sites 'one-for-one' inverts their meaning from 'hide from VoiceOver' to 'expose a description'. Ruling R-B correctly fixed the ownership defect (the counts existed nowhere); it did not validate the numbers. Both need re-deriving from `.testTag(` call sites and non-null `contentDescription` assignments before the registry is specified.

FR-32 (5.2-drivers.md:163) and FR-155 (5.8-data-sync.md:302) prescribe mutually exclusive handling of the same Backend Safety Limits payload, on an SI-11 surface, and no FR resolves the conflict. FR-32: 'Backend-supplied limits are clamped on write and clamped again on read ... A configuration of (minimum 450, maximum 300) resolves to (450, 451) — the minimum wins and the maximum is pushed up, never swapped. A maximum bolus of 0 resolves to 1.' FR-155: 'A Backend response carrying Alert Thresholds, a target glucose range, or Safety Limits that fails validation is DROPPED, never clamped, leaving last-known-good values in place ... Safety Limits reject min >= max, min outside 20-499, max outside 21-500, basal outside 1-15000 milliunits/hr, or bolus outside 1-25000 milliunits.' Each of FR-32's three worked examples is an input FR-155 rejects outright. FR-138 designates FR-32 as owner ('the clamp-on-write, clamp-on-read ordering that enforces this is owned by FR-32 and is not restated here'), but FR-155 restates a competing rule without deferring, and FR-81 applies the reject-whole posture to the sibling Alert Thresholds path. An implementer must guess, and the two behaviours differ materially in what a misconfigured Backend does to the live Glucose Validity window: FR-32 would apply a (450, 451) accept window (mitigated only by its own 'reported as a configuration fault' clause), FR-155 would keep last-known-good. One FR must own this and the other must defer by cross-reference.

Ruling R-E's defect class is not closed, and §7 now publishes a false completeness claim as a result. PL-57, PL-64 and PL-66 (7-parity-ledger.md:110, :117, :119) each name 'the published security-testing page (5.12)' as a disclosure surface; grep of 5.12-docs-policy.md returns no FR requiring such a page to exist — FR-219 through FR-237 require the docs contract, the install runbook, the Watch setup page, contributor docs, the security *disclosure policy*, the license surfaces, the disclaimer, the privacy document and the two troubleshooting pages, and none of them is a security-testing page. This violates §7's own preamble rule (line 5): 'Where the disclosure lives on a published documentation page, the row cites the FR that requires that page to exist and to carry the statement — never a page by name alone.' §7.4's opening sentence (line 221) — 'Every forced loss above names the product surface where the user is told, and every one of those surfaces is now required by an FR' — is therefore false as published, and is additionally self-contradicted six lines later at line 227, which records PL-3, PL-7, PL-38, PL-48 and PL-49 as having no user-facing disclosure at all. The cheapest fix §7.4 itself identifies is a consequence on FR-225 requiring a developer-section page recording the residual SAST, artifact-scanning and toolchain-trust gaps; the alternative is striking the page from the three cells and narrowing line 221's claim. Either way the completeness statement must stop being false before a downstream reader relies on it.

Until that row exists, FR-159's cross-reference resolves to nothing' — PD-45 (7-parity-ledger.md:189) records exactly that divergence, so the note is now factually wrong; 5.12-docs-policy.md:350-353 lists three 'still outstanding' items (§12/§16 scope statements, PL-63's disposition cell, FR-197's host list) that are all now applied.

FR-197 (5.11-engineering-gates.md:35) states flatly 'The roster is closed at five. No sixth Required Check is created', while §12.2 D-5 defers '`UI Tests (Simulator)` as a sixth Required Check' and FR-209 (:214) states 'promotion to required is a branch-protection change made once it proves stable'. FR-209 reconciles them, but FR-197's absolute phrasing reads as forbidding what D-5 explicitly defers. One clarifying clause in FR-197 ('closed at five for v1; any promotion is a branch-protection change, see FR-209 and D-5') removes the tension.

NFR-3 (6-nfrs.md:107-109) says the toolchain pin is 'enforced by the `iOS Gate` and `Workflow Lint` Required Checks (5.11 FR-208, FR-202)'. FR-202's three guards are actionlint+shellcheck, the 40-character SHA-pin guard and the composite-action secrets guard — none inspects an Xcode, macOS or Swift version. FR-208 alone enforces the pin. Not a host contradiction under R-C (FR-197 does map `Workflow Lint` to FR-202), but the claim reads stronger than FR-202 supports.

FR-193 (5.10-build-install.md:203) and FR-201 (5.11-engineering-gates.md:93) diverge in scope on package version pinning. FR-201: 'Every dependency is declared with `.exact(...)` or `.upToNextMinor(...)`; `branch:` and unbounded `.upToNextMajor(...)` are rejected for any cryptography- or Bluetooth-adjacent package.' FR-193: 'cryptography- and Bluetooth-adjacent packages are declared `.exact` or `.upToNextMinor`' — scoping the pinning rule itself narrowly. An architect reading FR-193 would permit `.upToNextMajor` on a non-crypto package; FR-201 forbids it. Compounding, FR-201 claims 'FR-193 defers here and does not restate them' while FR-193 restates the substance and appends 'See FR-201'.

§13 Success Metrics carries no NFR-10 battery measurement task with a named owner and a date. §12.2 D-8 correctly defers any published figure, which is half of what 6-nfrs.md's NFR-10 note asks for; the measurement-task half never landed, so nothing in the document says who runs the two-people-two-models protocol or by when. 6-nfrs.md:847-851 and its trailing open question state the choice precisely — either §13 gains the task or the PRD records explicitly that no figure ships in v1.

OQ-31 ('Is a shareable watch-face configuration file in scope for v1?') is substantively answered by §12.2 D-6, which defers it as optional with a revisit condition and now cross-links OQ-31 as the standing form of the question. This matches the D-5/OQ-52 pattern deliberately, but it means one live OQ duplicates a recorded deferral. Separately, §15:233-235 names the ten retired identifiers and the ten struck topics but does not map them one to one; the mapping of OQ-28, OQ-30 and OQ-44 to the graph Y axis, the Watch appearance preference and alert-history retention is not pinned anywhere and would need the pre-reconciliation draft to publish.

§10.2 (8-10-matrices.md:130) says 'The seven that survive the port are exactly the seven FR-197 enumerates as non-required'. That is a claim about ported jobs, not about the full non-required set, which also includes FR-194's auto-merge scope guard (no Android ancestor) plus the fork-side `Validate Secrets` and `Signing Smoke` that appear as rows in the same table. §10's preamble covers the class by rule, but the sentence reads as exhaustive.

FR-89 through FR-92 (the insulin surfaces) remain journey-orphaned — UJ-5 covers meals only, and 5.5's [NOTE FOR PM] at :248 flags it for a spine decision that has not been taken. Similarly 5.6's note at :317-320 records that AI Chat has no user journey. Both are deliberate flags, not defects, but a UX reader planning journey coverage should know the gap is intentional and unresolved.

New user-facing copy in FR-120 (5.7-watch.md:96-97) is invented rather than ported and carries no A-ID: the marker notation for a glyph whose tier is worse than the value's (`120 ->?` for a Stale glyph, `120 ?` for Too Stale/absent, with the rule that a marked glyph always keeps its direction character) and the accessibility phrasing 'trend stale' / 'trend unknown'. Android's 15-second poll meant its wrist never needed either. §16 should mint two Assumption entries if the PM wants them recorded for confirmation.

PD-46 (7-parity-ledger.md:190) states 'Exactly two gates, each with one bound, each pinned by its own test, and no clamping path anywhere.' In its glucose-validation context that is true, but two clamping paths do exist elsewhere and a reader scanning for the phrase will find them: FR-32 clamps Backend-supplied Safety Limits, and FR-125 (5.7-watch.md:159) clamps Alert Thresholds on the wrist in a dependent order. FR-125's clamp is display-banding-only and cannot arm an alert, so SI-5 holds; the wording should be scoped to glucose values.

5.8-data-sync.md:376-378's 'Open questions' block restates OQ-43 (per-Driver enqueue rate) and OQ-45 (the two ATS questions) in prose without citing their §15 identifiers, where 5.4 and 5.3 cite theirs by ID. Harmless to a machine; a reader cannot tell whether these are the same questions or new ones.
